setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.caption: Channel 1 plays a four-step melody through a MIDI device: trigs on steps 1 to 4 on pattern degrees 1 to 4 of scale slot 1 (C major), so MIDI notes 60, 62, 64 and 65. The channel octave is 0 and no step has an octave lock. The Device page is showing. The octave buttons sit along the bottom row, (8,8) for -2 up to (12,8) for +2, with (10,8) the written octave.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Turn E1 to Channel tasks, choose Trig params with E2 and press K3. With no step held, tap octave -2 at (8,8): the channel octave is -2 and the whole melody will drop two octaves. Hold step 2 and tap (8,8) too, then keep holding step 2: (8,8) is lit, showing that step's octave.
steps.title: Drop the channel two octaves, and lock step 2 to the same

steps.caption: Release step 2, press Play (1,8), then Stop. The MIDI strip reads 36, 38, 40 and 41 (C1, D1, E1, F1). A lock equal to the channel octave changes nothing you can hear. A low channel octave suits a bass line.
steps.title: A lock equal to the channel octave sounds the same

steps.caption: Hold step 2 and press K2 to clear its lock; play and stop, and all four steps follow the channel octave again. Then hold step 2 and tap octave -1 at (9,8), and keep it held: (9,8) lights while the step is held. Play, then Stop: step 2 sounds at MIDI 50, one octave above the channel setting, and the other steps stay at 36, 40 and 41.
steps.title: Lock step 2 one octave higher

steps.caption: Hold step 2, press K2 to clear its lock, play and stop. Then hold step 2 and tap octave 0 at (10,8). 0 is a lock like any other: step 2 returns to its written octave and sounds two octaves above its neighbours. MIDI 36, 62, 40 and 41.
steps.title: A local octave overrides the channel

steps.caption: Hold step 2 and press K2 to clear its octave lock. All four steps follow the channel octave -2 again: MIDI 36, 38, 40 and 41.
steps.title: K2 restores the channel octave

steps.caption: Hold step 2 and tap octave +1 at (11,8). Step 2 sounds at MIDI 74, an octave above its written note, while the other steps stay at 36, 40 and 41.
steps.title: Lock a step above the written octave

title: Place one step in another octave
